x: … as anyone and I'm sure that if Mel had any doubts about continuing his allegiance, Mary would be swift to dispel them! G.W. "Bill" Dance, who has only been a Belgravian for a few months is no newcomer to cross-country running.…

At the gun Bill Dance roared off into the lead at a pace that strung the field right out after one lap. Only three runners were with him at half a mile (2:15/13:30 pace!) - Joe Reilly, Adrian Major and Alan Black.

Bill Dance, now free from his achilles trouble, was all out for a trip to Belgium and forged through the field in the later stages. Blackheath and Ranelagh were almost at full strength yet only managed to beat our restricted team by 46 points and 6 points respectively.
Bill Dance was first to hit the top, with Gerry and Chris Steer close at hand; Bill and Ghris were to pay for their fast beginning, but we still had 8 in 25 and things looked well.
Bill Dance produced an excellent run, but broke down with achilles trouble next day so will have his work cut out to regain this form in time for the "Southern".
Team:- Gerry North (3), A.Fairclough (21), L.O'Hara (25), J.Bicourt (27), J.Thresher (28), G.Williams (33), T.Hart (39), G.Dance (43), B.Buxton (45).
Meanwhile Hart had retired ("the pace was too fast"), Bill Dance was another to pass the still unfit North and Peter Hilliar was suffering badly with stitch.
Dick Piotrowski held second place and although John Dear dropped to 6th on stage three they were still ahead of the 'A' outfit despite fine recovery efforts by Bill Dance and Gerry North.
Bill Dance on stage two was also not in his best form and was forced to drop a place although not losing ground on the leaders, Tipton, who had moved up from 3rd place.

Adrian Major ran exceptionally well to burn off Bill Dance, Derek Fernee and Tony Fairclough and gave best only to his captain. After his second placing in the '5¾' Jim Rimmer nearly caught the handicapper again with a praiseworthy 4th.

Stage 3 went to Bill Dance who pulled one right out of the bag and went through the field like the proverbial "dose of salts" to bring us into 7th place with a time which broke the previous stage record by 11 secs.

Bill Dance "relegated" to the 'B' team on this occasion, succeeded in putting the selectors to shame by soundly beating 'A' team runner Dick Piotrowski, albeit having only his second outing for us on the road.

Peter Whewell, Bill Dance and Gerry North stretched it to considerable proportions; the latter doing fastest time of the day. Laurie O'Hara finished off as usual, with Gerry Stevens (Reading) chasing him hard, but he had the race well under control and finished comfortably 16 seconds ahead of his rivals.
Adrian Major, 3rd in the mile, Bill Kerr and Gerry North, 2nd and 3rd in the 'three', and Bill Dance 2nd in the 'chase' were the highlights of Belgrave's 2nd placing behind T.V.H. - by just 3 points.
3000 metres S'Chase Although not living up to the promise of his earlier form, John Bicourt's 8:51.2 puts him ahead of Dick Piotrowski's 9:01.4 and Bill Dance's 9:27.8

As I mentioned in the March issue, it is sad that Bill Dance should have returned to the North. His desire to remain first claim and run for us, when he can,reflects his devotion to Belgrave and his enthusiasm for our team efforts.
Once the field had sorted itself out it appeared to the onlooker that the leading bunch were treating the heat with contempt; four of them, including Bill Dance, passing through 5 miles in 25m 24s!
Stage 6 saw Hercules make a strong bid for the lead with a record breaking run by Mike Beevor who started 58 secs behind Bill Dance and brought his team up to a mere 9 secs behind us.
1.R.Fowler (Staffs) 32:24; 22.G.W.Dance (Longwood) 35:24; 74.W.Laws 157.C.Henn; 172.G.Piddington (and will you just look who he beat...) 188.C.Walker.

Brother Gerry was back in good form after his set-back at Norwich but surprised even himself to run within 6 seconds of the record set by Geoff last year. Result: 1, Gerry North 27:20; 2, A.Fairclough 28:03; 3, G.W.Dance 28:07.
